comparator.name: Linguistics
comparator.sourceNotes: This example follows Language and Cognition in the Dutch-language track. The 120 EC major includes a capstone and thesis. The remaining 60 EC include a coherent elective package and other electives.

components.name: From Language to Linguistics
components.note: Introduces scientific approaches to studying human language.

components.name: Psychology of Language
components.note: Studies how people acquire and process language.

components.name: Comparative Morphosyntax
components.note: Compares word formation and sentence structure across languages.

components.name: Sociolinguistics
components.note: Studies language in its social contexts.

components.name: Digital Tools and Methods
components.note: Uses digital tools to investigate language.

components.name: Phonetics: The Study of Speech
components.note: Studies the production and perception of speech sounds.

components.name: Methods and Statistics
components.note: Develops research methods and statistical analysis for linguistics.

components.name: Phonology and Fieldwork
components.note: Examines sound systems and how to study them through fieldwork.

components.name: Experimental Psycholinguistics
components.note: Uses experiments to investigate language processing.

components.name: The Grammar of Words
components.note: Examines the internal structure of words.

components.name: Semantics and Pragmatics
components.note: Studies literal meaning and how context affects interpretation.

components.name: Language Acquisition and Language Structure
components.note: Examines language acquisition in relation to language structure.

components.name: Capstone Course Linguistics: Research, Writing and Reflection
components.note: Develops a research proposal and prepares students to write the thesis.

components.name: Linguistics Thesis
components.note: Students investigate a linguistic question and report their findings.

components.name: Coherent Elective Package
components.note: Choose a minor, a second specialization or approved study abroad.

components.name: Other Electives
components.note: Choose additional courses under Utrecht’s degree rules.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The three plans address distinct interests in language processing, language use in society, and computational approaches to language. All meet feasibility and pairwise distinctness. Each has a different balance of specialist language content and complementary disciplines.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both study how linguistic choices shape meaning. UCR approaches this through stylistics, dialogue and discourse.
Both examine human language processing. UCR covers experimental approaches alongside neuroscience, bilingualism and language disorders.
Utrecht introduces linguistics as a field of study.
Utrecht has a dedicated introduction to language psychology. UCR studies related processes in psycholinguistics and other cognition courses.
Utrecht compares how languages build words and sentences. UCR touches on these features in stylistics.
Utrecht studies how language develops. UCR offers broader developmental psychology and psycholinguistics.
Utrecht has a dedicated course on speech sounds and their production and perception.
Utrecht studies word structure in depth.
Utrecht has a dedicated course on semantics and pragmatics. UCR examines dialogue and language in context through stylistics.
Utrecht connects theories of language acquisition and grammatical structure.
Utrecht studies language variation in social settings. UCR approaches related questions through sociology and communication.
Both use digital methods to work with data. UCR covers general data analysis, including text data.
Both develop empirical research and statistical analysis. UCR uses examples from psychology.
Utrecht studies sound systems through linguistic fieldwork. UCR offers broader qualitative research methods.
Utrecht’s capstone develops a proposal for the required thesis.
Utrecht requires a thesis. UCR’s optional research element sits outside the scheduled degree.
This is a coherent elective package, such as a minor or a second specialization.
Students choose these electives under Utrecht’s degree rules.

notes.text: Utrecht’s degree includes a 120 EC major and 60 EC of electives. Half of the elective credits form a coherent package. Utrecht also requires a basic grammar test.
The UCR options share topics and methods with Utrecht. Utrecht has dedicated courses in phonetics, phonology, grammar and linguistic fieldwork, along with a required thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: Study how language works, how people acquire and understand it, and how it varies across communities. Utrecht offers Dutch- and English-language tracks. This example follows the Dutch track.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Utrecht example focuses on language and cognition. The UCR options emphasize cognition and communication, language and identity, or language data and AI.
